cards.b: GDP: total value of goods and services produced in a country in one year. Economic growth: an increase in GDP.
Growth, boom, recession, slump, then recovery.
A period of falling GDP lasting six months or more. Sales and profits fall, unemployment rises.

cards.f: Effect of a boom on businesses
cards.b: Demand is high, but costs (wages, materials) rise, recruitment is hard and inflation rises.
A general rise in prices in an economy. Raises business costs and cuts consumers' real incomes.
Changes in taxes and government spending.
Changes in the interest rate (and money supply), usually set by the central bank.

cards.f: Effect of higher interest rates on business
cards.b: Loan costs rise, less borrowing to expand, and consumers spend less (especially on goods bought on credit).
Make the economy more efficient: better education and training, privatisation, more competition, lower profit taxes.
External costs are paid by society (pollution, noise). Social cost = private costs + external costs.
Meeting the needs of the present without reducing the ability of future generations to meet theirs.
A group with a common interest that acts together to change policies of businesses or government (publicity, protests, boycotts).
The increasing worldwide trade and movement of people and capital between countries.
Tariff: a tax on imports. Quota: a limit on the quantity of a product that can be imported.
Strong currency: imports cheaper, exports dearer. A depreciation does the opposite: exports cheaper, imports dearer.

short.q: Explain how a rise in interest rates could affect a business that sells cars. [4]
short.model: Customers who buy on credit face higher repayments, so demand for cars falls. The business also pays more on any loans, so costs rise and profit falls.

short.q: Explain how a fall in the value of the euro affects a Spanish exporter selling in the USA. [3]
short.model: Each euro buys fewer dollars, so the exporter's goods become cheaper for American customers. This makes the exports more competitive and sales may rise.

short.q: A Spanish firm sells a product for €60 in the USA. Calculate the US price when €1 = USD 1.20. [2]
Explain one benefit and one cost to a business of reducing its pollution. [4]
short.model: Benefit: better brand image attracts green customers and lowers fines. Cost: cleaner equipment and materials are expensive, which may raise prices.

short.q: Explain how a government tariff on imported steel could affect a car maker that uses imported steel. [3]
short.model: The tariff makes imported steel dearer, so the car maker's costs rise and profit falls unless prices go up. Prices may then reduce sales.
